messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-8239 fired for service `gpu-runtime` — severity: P0. Condition: GPU memory pressure > 92% on node gpu-pool-13. link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-8239 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Escalation (lvl1 -> lvl2) sent to `eng-oncall` at 2026-03-14T02:21:18Z. Auto-retry in 30s.

alaa: seeing the PD alert. I’m on call, paging @samira and @jordan.

samira: acked. I’m connecting to the node. grabbing `nvidia-smi` output now.

mike: I’ll look at the runtime logs and recent deploys. last deploy for model-serving was ~20m ago.

jordan: taking ownership of mitigation. quick check — which customer traffic is hitting that pool?

alaa: enterprise-corp-prod and some canary traffic routed to this pool via routing policy `route:v1`.

samira: nvidia-smi snapshot:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 528.49       Driver Version: 535.54.03    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| Fan  Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap| Memory-Usage | GPU-Util  Compute M. |
| 0   A100-SXM8-40GB  On        | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                    0 |
| 40%  82C  P2   250W / 400W   | 39122MiB / 40960MiB | 99%     Default     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
samira: GPU memory ~39GB/40GB, processes look like many small inference workers with large batch windows.

mike: runtime logs (tail):
```
2026-03-14T02:10:45Z ERROR runtime: cudaAlloc returned out of memory
2026-03-14T02:10:46Z WARN  runtime: retrying allocation (attempt 1)
2026-03-14T02:11:02Z ERROR runtime: failed to allocate KV cache for request 0x7f9c...
```

jordan: hypothesis: an incoming spike of batched requests pushed aggregate memory > quantized profile. Could be steady-state increase + a sudden canary load.

nina: I’m seeing elevated 5xx rates for enterprise-corp in Grafana -> 12% errors over 5m, latency p95 spikes to 4.8s. Can confirm customer-facing impact.

alaa: mitigation options: 1) scale down batch_size at router for this pool, 2) drain node and restart pods, 3) fallback to smaller model variant (quantized), 4) route enterprise-corp to dedicated pool if available.

jordan: start with non-disruptive controls first — reduce batch_size and enable kv-cache eviction. Applying routing override for `gpu-pool-13` to `batch_size=1` and `kv_cache_ttl=30s` for now.

samira: running command on control plane:
```
# apply routing override
redwoodctl routing set --pool gpu-pool-13 --override "batch_size=1,kv_cache_ttl=30s"
```
samira: override applied. watching memory.

(45s later)

samira: GPU memory dropped to ~28GB. process count down. Errors decreased to ~3.2%. latency p95 now 2.2s.

mike: still seeing some allocation failures from an older shard: `runtime/pool_shard_7`. I’m going to cordon node gpu-pool-13 and evict pods to rotate them. Requesting brief capacity dip.

alaa: ok to cordon. inform customers? We have a small impact window but we should announce to affected tenants.

jordan: cordon + drain in progress:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-pool-13
kubectl drain gpu-pool-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

nina: sending heads-up to SRE channel and to customer success for enterprise-corp. Draft: "We’ve detected GPU memory pressure impacting a subset of requests; mitigation underway (routing override + node rotation). Possible short errors/latency"

pagerduty-bot: PD-8239 acknowledged by `samira` at 2026-03-14T02:24:55Z. Escalation timers paused.

mike: pods rescheduled onto gpu-pool-8 and gpu-pool-9. Observability: memory usage per pod returned to expected baseline. No more OOM logs in last 4m.

alaa: good recovery. Remaining actions: schedule postmortem, identify root cause (regression in batching logic? model change?), check why kv-cache eviction wasn't earlier, consider autoscaling rules.

jordan: initial RCA pointers: a recent change in the request aggregator increased max_batch_window from 100ms to 400ms for throughput experiment; that allowed larger per-batch sequence combinations exceeding quantized memory expectation. I’ll open an incident-ticket.

samira: creating incident ticket now: INC-2026-0314-GPU-MEM. Assign SRE + runtime-ml + oncall. Summary includes timestamps, mitigation commands, customer impact metrics.

mike: note for postmortem: add a test that runs an integration of aggregator change against memory profiles for quantized models. Also consider a hard cap at routing layer.

alaa: handoff — I’ll remain on for 30 minutes then hand to next oncall `nina` at 03:00 UTC. If anything regresses, re-open PD.

nina: acked for handoff. I’ll follow up with CS for an ETA note to enterprise-corp and track the incident through postmortem.

(1h later)

samira: follow-up: root cause confirmed — aggregator window change was rolled in canary; combined with a rare sequence length distribution in enterprise-corp leads to per-batch memory blowout. Fix: revert window change and add batching guardrails.

alaa: resolution notes: routing override removed after fix rolled and nodes stabilized. PD incident PD-8239 resolved at 2026-03-14T03:21:50Z. No further OOMs.

jordan: action items assigned in INC-2026-0314-GPU-MEM: (1) add autotest for batch memory, (2) add runtime soft-limits, (3) improve alerting thresholds to consider batch_size changes, (4) customer follow-up doc.

nina: copied to #postmortems and assigned to `samira` and `mike`. Closing thread but leaving ticket open until postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:
